summary: Intermittent wake-from-suspend on Framework Laptop 13 due to lid sensor firmware misreporting
description:
Issue summary: Multiple engineers reported laptops failing to remain suspended overnight. Machines appear to enter suspend but then immediately wake (10-30s) and stay on. This is impacting developer workstations and our overnight build agents on Framework Laptop 13 devices.

Observed scope: Reports started 2026-02-28; ~7 confirmed devices in Engineering and Infra teams. Problem is intermittent but reproducible on affected firmware revisions.

Business impact: Developer disruption, increased power usage for remote workers, flaky CI runners that rely on suspend for power management. Not customer-facing but affects SRE/dev productivity.
impact: ~7 developer machines + 2 runner hosts observed; increases power drain and causes processes that expect long suspend to fail. No data loss reported. Priority elevated due to CI runner disruption.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Boot Framework Laptop 13 with stock Redwood engineer image (ubuntu-22.04-custom) and firmware EC v1.1.3.
2) Leave machine idle for 5 minutes, then trigger system suspend (systemctl suspend) or close lid.
3) Observe that the machine wakes after ~10-30s and remains active. Reopening lid is not required for wake event.
4) Check ACPI events and journalctl logs for wake source.
observed_logs: Mar 01 08:12:45 workstation-019 kernel: PM: suspend entry (deep)
Mar 01 08:12:55 workstation-019 kernel: wakeup source: LID (EC) - event 0x23
Mar 01 08:12:55 workstation-019 systemd[1]: Started User Manager for UID 1001.
Mar 01 08:12:55 workstation-019 kernel: ACPI: Lid Switch (PECI) reported open -> closed (value 0x1)
Mar 01 08:12:56 workstation-019 kernel: PM: Device X triggered wakeup: gpio-ioexpander-ec:gpio13
investigation_notes: Initial triage (2026-03-01): Reproduced locally on a test Framework 13 with EC firmware v1.1.3. Suspected EC/lid debounce logic introduced in recent firmware change.
Cross-check: Identical image on Lenovo X1 and Dell Precision reproduced no wake behavior, pointing to vendor EC firmware as common factor.
/proc/acpi/button/lid/LID/state showed rapid toggling in the short suspend window on affected machines; wakeup source consistently reports EC GPIO pin.
Tried kernel parameter 'acpi_osi=' and 'acpi_enforce_resources=lax' — no change. Disabling autosuspend for USB devices did not affect behavior.
Infra tried imaging latest nightly (ubuntu-24.04-beta) — still reproduced with EC v1.1.3. Suggests not an OS regression.
Contacted vendor (Framework) support and opened internal Slack thread #it-support; vendor acknowledged a known EC debounce regression in v1.1.3 and provided EC v1.1.5 candidate.
Vendor provided test EC firmware v1.1.5 addressing lid-debounce and pin state reporting. Applied to two test devices; neither exhibited spur wakes after multiple suspend cycles.
Risk assessment: Firmware update touches EC; packaged deployment to all engineers should be scheduled with consent and backup steps.
actions_taken: Applied vendor test EC firmware v1.1.5 to two affected laptops (Priya N). Performed 20 suspend/resume cycles overnight — no unexpected wakes.
Temporarily applied workaround for affected CI runners: set 'HandleLidSwitch=ignore' and mask systemd-logind suspend triggers to prevent flaky wake affecting jobs.
Notified Engineering via #it-support with detection script to list EC firmware versions (script attached in Slack).
Prepared step-by-step EC flash runbook and rollback instructions. Added check to asset DB to flag devices running v1.1.3.
Opened internal GitHub PR to include EC firmware v1.1.5 in our provisioning image build: https://github.com/redwood-inference/firmware-updates/pull/128
resolution:
Root cause: EC firmware v1.1.3 on Framework Laptop 13 has a debounce/regression causing spurious lid open/close events during suspend, triggering wakeups. Fix: vendor-supplied EC firmware v1.1.5 corrects debounce behavior.

Resolution steps: Applied v1.1.5 to affected machines and rolled out a staged firmware update to remaining flagged devices (opt-in schedule for developers). Updated provisioning image to include v1.1.5. Workaround (HandleLidSwitch=ignore) used for CI runners until firmware applied. Ticket closed after 48 hours of stable verification on updated devices.
